typical_wishbone_read_sequence_classic_s: 1. MASTER drives [ADR_O()]=A, [TGA_O()]=valid, negates [WE_O] (READ), drives [SEL_O()]=valid byte-lanes, asserts [CYC_O] (+ optional [TGC_O], [LOCK_O]).
2. MASTER asserts [STB_O] at the same rising [CLK_I] or later — starts the request phase.
3. SLAVE decodes the address (partial or full decode), drives valid [DAT_I()] + [TGD_I()] and asserts [ACK_I] (or inserts SLAVE wait state -WSS- by holding [ACK_O]=0 for one or more cycles).
4. At the next rising [CLK_I] with [ACK_I]=1, MASTER latches read data and negates [STB_O] and [CYC_O].
5. SLAVE negates [ACK_O] in response to negated [STB_I].
typical_wishbone_write_sequence_classic_: 3. SLAVE prepares to latch DAT_O+TGD_O on next rising [CLK_I]; SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] (or inserts wait state).
4. At the next rising [CLK_I] with [ACK_I]=1, SLAVE latches write data, MASTER negates [STB_O] and [CYC_O].
typical_wishbone_block_read_sequence: 2. For each of N phases: MASTER drives [ADR_O()]=Ak + [SEL_O()] + [TGA_O()], asserts [STB_O]; SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] with [DAT_I()]=Dk; MASTER latches data and (optionally) negates [STB_O] to insert a master wait state (-WSM-) before the next phase.
3. After the last phase's data latched, MASTER negates [STB_O] AND [CYC_O] ending the block.
Throughout the block, [CYC_O] remains asserted — defines the BLOCK as one indivisible-from-arbitration unit (combined with [LOCK_O] if needed).
typical_wishbone_block_write_sequence: Same as BLOCK READ but with [WE_O]=1 throughout and [DAT_O()]=Dk driven by MASTER on each phase.
typical_wishbone_rmw_sequence: 3. MASTER negates [STB_O] (-WSM- between halves) BUT KEEPS [CYC_O] asserted — atomic.
4. WRITE half: MASTER asserts [WE_O]=1, drives [DAT_O()]=Modified, asserts [STB_O].
5. SLAVE asserts [ACK_I]; SLAVE latches write data.
6. MASTER negates [STB_O] AND [CYC_O] ending the cycle — the SLAVE never released arbitration between the read and write halves.
registered_feedback_classic_sequence_cti: 2. SLAVE recognizes Classic cycle, asserts [ACK_I] with data; MASTER terminates as in standard Classic.
registered_feedback_constant_address_bur: 1. MASTER drives [ADR_O()]=A (constant), [CTI_O()]=3'b001, [WE_O]=R/W, [SEL_O()], [CYC_O]=1, [STB_O]=1; SLAVE captures burst type.
2. For each beat k>=0: SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] with [DAT_I()]=Data_k (or accepts [DAT_O()]=Data_k on write); MASTER MAY pulse [STB_O] for each beat.
3. On the LAST beat: MASTER drives [CTI_O()]=3'b111 (End-of-Burst) together with [STB_O] for that beat.
registered_feedback_incrementing_burst_s: 1. MASTER drives [ADR_O()]=A_start, [CTI_O()]=3'b010, [BTE_O()]=wrap-mode (Linear/Wrap-4/Wrap-8/Wrap-16), [WE_O], [SEL_O()], [CYC_O]=1, [STB_O]=1; SLAVE captures burst type and wrap mode.
2. For each beat k>=1: MASTER drives next [ADR_O()] per Table 4-3 (incremented per data array size, modulo the wrap boundary); SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] with read or write data.
3. On the LAST beat: MASTER drives [CTI_O()]=3'b111 (End-of-Burst); SLAVE recognizes End-of-Burst.
pipelined_classic_sequence: 2. If [STALL_I]=0 at rising [CLK_I], request is accepted; MASTER drives next request (A1) on the next cycle.
3. If [STALL_I]=1, MASTER holds the request (does NOT advance to next address).
4. SLAVE asserts [ACK_I] for each completed request; for reads, drives valid [DAT_I()] at the cycle of [ACK_I]=1.
5. After all requests issued and the last [ACK_I] received, MASTER negates [CYC_O] (Section 3.1.3.2 — cycle of N transactions ends after N ACKs).
error_termination_sequence_err: 1. MASTER initiates a cycle as usual ([CYC_O]=1, [STB_O]=1).
2. SLAVE detects an error condition (e.g. parity fault, address not decoded, watchdog timeout).
3. SLAVE asserts [ERR_O]=1 (instead of [ACK_O]); SLAVE MUST NOT assert [ACK_O] or [RTY_O] at the same time (RULE 3.45).
4. MASTER detects [ERR_I]=1 at the next rising [CLK_I], terminates the cycle (negates [STB_O] AND [CYC_O]); IP-supplier-defined response (re-issue, trap to processor, log fault, etc.).
5. SLAVE negates [ERR_O] in response to negated [STB_I].
retry_termination_sequence_rty: 1. MASTER initiates a cycle as usual.
2. SLAVE is temporarily busy (shared-memory contention, bridge backed up, etc.).
4. MASTER detects [RTY_I]=1, terminates the cycle (negates [STB_O] AND [CYC_O]); the cycle SHOULD be retried later (IP-supplier-defined timing).

ordering_rules_summary.wishbone_single_master_classic: Single-MASTER Wishbone Classic is strictly in-order (handshake protocol implies one outstanding transfer at a time).
ordering_rules_summary.wishbone_single_master_pipelined: Single-MASTER Wishbone Pipelined: requests are issued in order; ACKs come back in order (slave-pipeline FIFO behavior).
ordering_rules_summary.wishbone_block_burst_order: All phases of a BLOCK or Registered Feedback burst are sequential; addresses follow Section 3.5 ordering (BIG/LITTLE ENDIAN) and Section 4.4.4 / Table 4-3 (Linear/Wrap-4/Wrap-8/Wrap-16) for incrementing bursts.
ordering_rules_summary.wishbone_multi_master: Multi-MASTER systems require an INTERCON with arbitration; arbitration policy is end-user-defined (priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter, etc.).
ordering_rules_summary.wishbone_lock: [LOCK_O] guarantees the bus is not granted to any other MASTER between the assertion of [LOCK_O] and the negation of [LOCK_O] or [CYC_O].

fields.narrow_transfer_sequence: Wishbone supports narrow transfers via [SEL_O()] byte-lane selection. Active [SEL_O()] bits qualify the corresponding byte-lanes of [DAT_O()] (write) and [DAT_I()] (read). Section 3.5 figures (3-15..3-21) define byte-lane addressing for 8/16/32/64-bit ports for both BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN.
fields.early_burst_termination: A Registered Feedback burst is terminated by the MASTER asserting [CTI_O()]=3'b111 (End-of-Burst) on the cycle of the last beat. A Classic BLOCK or RMW cycle is terminated by the MASTER negating [STB_O] AND [CYC_O] at the end of the last phase. SLAVE-initiated early termination is possible via [ERR_O] or [RTY_O].

evidence.quote: MASTER drives address+control+CYC_O+TGC_O; asserts STB_O; SLAVE asserts ACK_I with valid DAT_I and TGD_I (with optional SLAVE wait states); MASTER latches data, negates STB_O and CYC_O.
MASTER drives address+write-data+WE_O+SEL_O+CYC_O+TGC_O+STB_O; SLAVE asserts ACK_I (with wait states optional); MASTER negates STB_O and CYC_O.

BLOCK cycles wrap multiple phases inside a single sustained CYC_O. Each phase follows the same STB_O+ACK_I handshake as the SINGLE cycle. CYC_O signal can be used to request permission to access a shared resource from a local arbiter; to hold the access until the end of the cycle the [LOCK_O] signal must be asserted.
RMW: single read data transfer in first half; single write data transfer in second half; CYC_O remains asserted during both halves.
Cycle consisting of N transactions is terminated with a sequence of N ACK_I. Master terminates the bus cycle (by deasserting CYC_O) after receiving the last ACK_I pulse.

Classic Cycle (CTI_O=000): identical to Wishbone Classic. End-Of-Burst (CTI_O=111): asserted on the last beat. Constant Address Burst Cycle (CTI_O=001): multiple beats with same ADR_O. Incrementing Burst Cycle (CTI_O=010): linear / 4-wrap / 8-wrap / 16-wrap selected by BTE_O.
ERR_I indicates abnormal cycle termination; RTY_I indicates cycle should be retried; LOCK_O when asserted, indicates that the current bus cycle is uninterruptible.
